questions.heading: Activity Bounds Prove a Row Redundant or Fix a Variable
questions.stem: A row reads 5a + 4b + 2c <= 8 over binaries, and an earlier reduction fixed b = 1. What can presolve conclude from this row alone?

options.text: The row is redundant, since its least activity 4 is under 8
options.says: Redundant needs the most activity under 8; here it is 11, so the row can still bind.

options.text: The model is infeasible, since its most activity 11 is over 8
options.says: Infeasible needs the least activity over 8; the least is 4, and plans with a = 0 fit.

options.text: a is fixed at 0, since b's 4 plus a's 5 is over the 8
options.says: Right: the least activity is 4, and 4 + 5 = 9 > 8, so a = 1 can never fit.

options.text: c is fixed at 0, since b's 4 plus c's 2 leaves no room for a
options.says: 4 + 2 = 6 fits under 8; the rule asks whether c fits with the least activity, not with a.

questions.heading: A Variable That Only Helps Is Set to Its Best Value
questions.stem: A maximization has only <= rows. Project q is worth 300 and appears in one row, x_r - x_q <= 0 (project r needs q). What does dual fixing do with x_q?

options.text: Fixes it at 1, since raising it adds value and only loosens its row
options.says: Right: value 300 > 0 and its one coefficient is -1, so x_q = 1 is never worse.

options.text: Fixes it at 0, since its negative entry marks it as a cost to the row
options.says: A negative entry in a <= row means raising x_q makes room in the row, not that it costs.

options.text: Leaves it free, since a precedence row links it to another project
options.says: Dual fixing looks only at signs: a parent's -1 in a precedence row does not stop it.

options.text: Removes its row, since a row with a negative entry can never bind
options.says: The row binds whenever x_r = 1; a row is removed only when its most activity fits.

questions.heading: Coefficient Tightening Makes the LP Bound Tighter Without Changing Any Plan
questions.stem: Presolve applies coefficient tightening to a's coefficient in the row 7a + 2b + 2c <= 8 over free binaries. Which row does it produce?

options.text: 7a + 2b + 2c <= 4, since the right-hand side alone drops by 4
options.says: This removes the plan a = 1 alone, which the original row allows (7 <= 8).

options.text: 3a + 2b + 2c <= 8, since a's coefficient alone drops by 4
options.says: This allows a = b = c = 1 (7 <= 8), a plan the original row refuses (11 > 8).

options.text: 5a + 2b + 2c <= 6, since both drop by the 2 that b leaves
options.says: d is b minus the most activity without a: 8 - (2 + 2) = 4, not 2.

options.text: 3a + 2b + 2c <= 4, since both drop by the 4 left without a
options.says: Right: without a the row holds at most 4, so d = 8 - 4 = 4 comes off a and off the right-hand side.
